tools.name: check_domains
tools.description: Check the registration status of one or more domains — whether each is taken, expiring, in redemption, in pendingDelete, or available to register. Returns status, expiry, registrar, name servers, EPP codes, and a buyer-focused drop forecast (predicted release window and confidence) for names in thei

tools.name: check_name
tools.description: Name Safety Check for a brand name: domain availability across .com/.io/.ai/.app/.dev/.co, social-handle availability (best effort), and a US trademark knockout search of public USPTO records. Returns structured results. This is a knockout search, not legal advice. No authentication required.

tools.name: watch_domains
tools.description: Add one or more domains to your snooze watchlist. Each is monitored continuously and you get an email when its status changes or it nears a drop. Requires signing in to your snooze account. Up to 25 domains per call (100 total).

tools.name: unwatch_domains
tools.description: Remove one or more domains from your snooze watchlist. Requires signing in to your snooze account.

tools.name: list_watches
tools.description: List every domain on your snooze watchlist with its current status and drop forecast — so an agent can see what it is already tracking. Requires signing in to your snooze account.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: watch_domains · Private data: check_name · Public sink: watch_domains · Destructive: check_domains, watch_domains, unwatch_domains, list_watches.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: watch_domains · Private data: check_name · Public sink: watch_domains · Destructive: check_domains, watch_domains, unwatch_domains, list_watches

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
